title: The Era of Magic
subtitle: The few years since magic was found, and the odd order it was found in
summary: What newspapers call the years since magic started coming out of the Gates. It is only a few years old, and it happened in the wrong order: Runes, then Forms, then the Words, and only last a way to cast without a Rune.
content:
> *"Nobody invented magic. We found it lying about, and have been trying to read the instructions ever since."*
> — said in the University laboratories in Endros

The **Era of Magic** is what newspapers call the few years since magic began. Before the [[gates|Gates]] the world had none: the faiths had their miracles and arguments, and natural philosophers had nothing to measure. The phrase makes it sound settled and grand. It's neither. The first textbooks are still being written.

What matters most is the order things were found in, because it's not the order a textbook would choose:

1. **[[runes-of-the-gates|Runes]]**, artifacts from the Gates that could make an impossible effect happen again, though nobody understood them.
2. **[[forms|Forms]]**: Professor [Manhattan R. Wylde](characters.html#manhattan-wylde) of the University of Verna made a pearl glow on purpose with **Effect Glowing**, and published how. Two more Forms followed fast, and a rush began: universities, governments, industrial laboratories, patrons and Expeditioners all wanted to find the next one.
3. **[[words|Words]]**: comparing the Forms against the Runes showed what each Rune actually supplied.
4. **[[base-form|Base Form]]**: last of all, a way to manifest a Word without a Rune.

Spellcasting was usable before it was understood, and understood before anyone could do it unaided. The big open questions (why the universe answers at all, what a Rune is, whether people can make one) are research questions, and the history is short enough that an Expeditioner could write the next chapter. The rules are on the Rules page: [Spellcasting](game.html#post-spellcasting).
